title: disruption objectives dependencies
question: Can a service meet its RTO yet fail its RPO or MTD/MAD constraint because a dependency or usable-data checkpoint is late?
scenario: Emergency claims intake: A claims service can tolerate a short delay but cannot lose submitted emergency cases.
focalRelation: RTO measures service-restoration elapsed time forward from disruption; RPO measures recoverable-data age backward from disruption; MTD/MAD bounds tolerable disruption; end-to-end capability also requires named dependencies.

prediction.prompt: Can a service meet its RTO yet fail its RPO or MTD/MAD constraint because a dependency or usable-data checkpoint is late?

options.label: Test data loss, restore time, tolerable disruption, and dependencies separately.
options.feedback: A restored server may meet elapsed-time target while the data is too old or the process remains unusable.

options.label: Declare recovery successful from zero data loss without checking elapsed restoration or tolerable disruption.
options.feedback: Zero data loss can meet RPO while service restoration still misses RTO and maximum tolerable disruption.

options.label: Treat a zero-loss restore as proof that RPO, RTO, MTD, and dependency targets all passed.
options.feedback: Zero loss addresses RPO; elapsed restoration and tolerable disruption still require separate RTO and MTD/MAD checks.

prediction.hint: Compare data loss with RPO and usable business acceptance with RTO; restoration alone is not acceptance.

transfer.prompt: The service is usable seven hours after disruption with zero data loss; its RTO is four hours and MTD/MAD is six hours.

options.label: RPO is met, but RTO is missed and the six-hour maximum tolerable disruption is exceeded
options.feedback: RPO is met, but RTO is missed and the six-hour maximum tolerable disruption is exceeded; zero loss does not rescue the time failures.

options.label: Declare full recovery success because zero data loss meets RPO, without checking the seven-hour acceptance time.
options.feedback: Zero data loss can meet RPO while service restoration still misses RTO and maximum tolerable disruption. Recompute the decision from Observed recovery time is 7 hours. Observed data loss is 0 hours. RTO is 4 hours and MTD/MAD is 6 hours.

options.label: Treat zero-loss restoration as passing every objective even though usable service arrives after RTO and MTD.
options.feedback: Zero loss addresses RPO; elapsed restoration and tolerable disruption still require separate RTO and MTD/MAD checks. In this case, observed recovery time is 7 hours; observed data loss is 0 hours; rTO is 4 hours and MTD/MAD is 6 hours.

transfer.hint: Recompute the data-loss and elapsed-time tests separately from the changed timestamps.

retry.prompt: A cloud application has replicas but depends on a single external identity provider. What should the continuity review highlight?

options.label: Treat the identity provider as an end-to-end recovery dependency
options.feedback: Correct. Service recovery depends on the end-to-end chain, not only application replicas.

options.label: Treat the application replicas and database backup as a complete continuity plan without identity recovery.
options.feedback: Recovery also needs priorities, people, procedures, dependencies, communication, and tested restoration capability.

options.label: Declare the service recoverable from replica health alone and leave external identity-provider recovery untested.
options.feedback: That shortcut ignores the decisive changed fact. Service recovery depends on the end-to-end chain, not only application replicas.

retry.hint: A current recovery point can pass RPO while late service acceptance still misses RTO and MTD.

takeaway: Use the case evidence to apply this relation: RTO measures service-restoration elapsed time forward from disruption; RPO measures recoverable-data age backward from disruption; MTD/MAD bounds tolerable disruption; end-to-end capability also requires named dependencies.
assumptions: Only entities and claims anchored in the canonical unit or explicitly labeled hypothetical scenario are used.
A highlighted path means the learner is inspecting that path; it does not assert the event occurred.
The current source is authoritative for facts; this treatment reorganizes presentation without changing canonical content.
The lesson teaches one bounded decision and does not claim to exhaust every jurisdiction, vendor implementation, architecture, attack, or exception.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The quantitative timeline preserves the recoverable point, disruption, technical restoration, business acceptance, RPO, RTO, and maximum tolerable disruption on one scale, and the changed case moves those values independently. Dependency restoration is explained through the technical-to-business acceptance relation rather than a separate reviewed dependency strip, so the treatment is equivalent.

quantitative.description: The one-hour-old snapshot misses the fifteen-minute RPO. Technical restoration at three hours becomes usable after business acceptance at 3.5 hours, meeting the four-hour RTO and staying within the six-hour maximum tolerable disruption.
